title: Event and Venue Booking Agreement
summary: Book a venue or event space with dates, fees, deposits, cancellation and house rules.
useWhen: A venue rents its space to a client for a private event, performance, meeting or party.
watchOuts: Alcohol: the venue or a licensed caterer usually must hold the liquor license. Hosts can face liability for serving intoxicated guests (dram shop and social host laws), and venues often require liquor liability insurance.
Capacity limits come from the fire code and the venue's certificate of occupancy, not the contract.
Cancellation: courts may refuse to enforce a cancellation fee that is a penalty rather than a reasonable estimate of the venue's loss. Use a graduated schedule.
Music played at public events may require PRO licenses (ASCAP, BMI, SESAC, GMR). Venues usually hold them, but check.

variables.label: Venue: full legal name
variables.help: Full legal name of the person, or the exact registered name of the company.

variables.label: Client: full legal name
variables.help: Full legal name of the person, or the exact registered name of the company.

variables.label: Space rented
variables.help: Room or area and venue address.

variables.label: Expected guests
variables.help: Must not exceed the legal capacity.

variables.label: What's included
variables.default: Tables, chairs, restrooms, basic lighting and on-site staff contact.

variables.label: Cancellation schedule
variables.default:
- More than 90 days before the event: deposit refunded minus $100.
- 30 to 90 days before: deposit kept.
- Less than 30 days before: 100% of the rental fee is owed.
variables.help: What the client owes if they cancel.

variables.label: Client must carry event insurance?
variables.help: Event liability insurance naming the venue.

variables.label: House rules
variables.default: No confetti, glitter or open flames except candles in enclosed holders. Amplified music ends at 10:00 p.m. All decorations removed by the end of the access period.

variables.label: Governing law (state)
variables.help: Two-letter code of the state whose law governs this agreement. Usually where the parties or the work are located.

sections.title: 2. Booking
sections.body: Venue reserves {{space}} for Client's {{event_type}} on {{event_date}}, with access from {{access_time}}, for up to {{guest_count}} guests. Client will not exceed the lawful capacity of the space.

sections.title: 4. Fees and payment
sections.body: The rental fee is {{rental_fee}}. Client pays a deposit of {{deposit}} at signing, which is applied to the fee, and the balance by {{balance_due}}. Client also pays a refundable damage deposit of {{damage_deposit}}, returned within 14 days after the event minus documented costs of damage, extra cleaning or overtime. If the balance is not paid on time, Venue may cancel the booking under the cancellation terms.

sections.title: 5. Cancellation by Client
sections.body:
Client may cancel in writing. The parties agree the following reflects a reasonable estimate of Venue's loss:

{{cancel_schedule}}

sections.title: 6. Cancellation by Venue and events outside anyone's control
sections.body: If Venue cannot provide the space for reasons within its control, it will refund all payments. If fire, severe weather, natural disaster, government order, utility failure or similar events outside either party's control prevent the event, either party may cancel, and Venue will refund payments minus documented, non-recoverable costs it has already incurred, or offer a substitute date.

sections.title: 7. House rules and conduct
sections.body:
{{house_rules}}

Client is responsible for the conduct of its guests and vendors, and for compliance with Venue's rules and the law. Venue may stop the event or remove people whose conduct is unsafe or unlawful.

sections.title: 8. Vendors
sections.body: Client's outside vendors, such as caterers, DJs and decorators, must follow Venue's rules and provide proof of insurance if Venue asks.

sections.title: 9. Alcohol
sections.body: Alcohol may be served only by a licensed bartender or caterer approved by Venue, or by Venue itself, in compliance with all liquor laws. No one under 21 will be served. Venue or its bartender may refuse service to anyone who appears intoxicated. Client will not allow guests to bring their own alcohol unless Venue agrees in writing.

sections.title: 10. Insurance
sections.body: Client will carry event liability insurance of at least {{insurance_amount}} per occurrence (including liquor liability if alcohol is served), naming Venue as an additional insured, and provide a certificate at least 14 days before the event.

sections.title: 11. Damage and liability
sections.body: Client will pay for damage to the venue caused by Client, its guests or vendors, beyond normal wear. Client will indemnify Venue against claims arising from the event, except claims caused by Venue's negligence or willful misconduct. Venue is not responsible for items left at the venue.

sections.title: 12. General terms
sections.body:
- **Whole agreement.** This document (with any attachments named in it) is the parties' entire agreement on its subject and replaces earlier discussions and drafts.
- **Changes.** It can only be changed in a writing signed by all parties.
- **Severability.** If a court finds any part unenforceable, that part is limited to the minimum extent needed and the rest stays in effect.
- **No waiver.** Not enforcing a term once is not a waiver of it later.
- **Notices.** Notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, by a recognized courier, by certified mail, or by email to the addresses in this document (or a later address a party gives in writing). Email notice is effective when sent unless the sender receives a bounce-back.
- **Governing law.** The law of the state of {{governing_state}} governs this agreement, without regard to conflict-of-law rules.
- **Counterparts and electronic signatures.** This agreement may be signed in counterparts and electronically. Each party consents to doing business electronically under the federal E-SIGN Act and the state's version of the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act (or New York's Electronic Signatures and Records Act). An electronic signature has the same effect as a handwritten one.

sections.title: Signatures
sections.body:
By signing below, each party agrees to this document.

**Venue** — {{venue_name}}

[[sig:venue]]

Printed name: [[name:venue]]
Title (if signing for a company): [[text:venue:Title]]
Date: [[date:venue]]

**Client** — {{client_name}}

[[sig:client]]

Printed name: [[name:client]]
Title (if signing for a company): [[text:client:Title]]
Date: [[date:client]]
